retirement_rule: Retire a Base44 dependency only after its named replacement is live, independently verified, reconciled and rollback-safe.

app_fabric_compatibility.boundary: Compatibility covers observed Base44 SDK call geometry. Product-specific unsupported calls and hard-coded legacy routes remain explicit migration blockers.

canonical_data.boundary: Higher-volume or distributed workloads require a stronger backing implementation behind the same compatibility contract before cutover.

identity_boundary.boundary: Identity and session issuance are owned. Registration/recovery remain fail-closed until a real delivery adapter returns a receipt. Legacy credentials are not copied.

realtime_bus.boundary: Durable hash-chained sequence log plus authorized resumable SSE baseline. Product-specific realtime semantics still require parity.

secret_store.boundary: Master encryption key is supplied out of band and is never persisted by the store. Provider credentials are re-issued rather than copied from Base44.

object_storage.boundary: Content-addressed local baseline with app-scoped references and integrity checks. Replication and geographic requirements remain app-specific cutover gates.

source_dependency_scanner.boundary: Scans extracted source for migration dependencies while redacting cross-app identifiers, environment values and hard-coded legacy route values.

lossless_entity_transfer.boundary: Requires terminal pagination, immutable page hashes, whole-stream reconciliation, idempotent import and destination field verification. Transfer receipts do not authorize traffic cutover.

identity_challenge_broker.boundary: Pending registration credentials are encrypted; OTPs and reset tokens are hash-only at rest. No successful delivery state exists without a delivery receipt.

receipt_gated_route_registry.boundary: A destination may be staged and verified without receiving traffic. Activation requires a separate cutover receipt pinned to the verified route binding and release. Raw legacy route values are fingerprinted rather than persisted.

owned_runtime_base44_network_firewall.boundary: Critical owned runtime surfaces may contain compatibility terminology but may not hard-code Base44 network destinations.

estate_coverage_ledger.boundary: Coverage uses source-ID fingerprints, withholds unmatched source names and never treats the capped 100-app listing as proof of complete inventory. Untitled sources require classification before migration or archive; aliases require authority receipts.

connector_gateway.boundary: Provider credentials are re-authorized through owned one-time OAuth state. State is hash-only at rest, new redirect URIs must be owned/non-Base44, and credential values remain in Evercraft Secret Store.

webhook_gateway.boundary: Inbound events use raw-body signature verification, bounded replay windows, idempotent event ledgers and payload-free receipts. Provider-side webhook repointing remains a separate verified migration action.

integration_edge.boundary: Provides owned OAuth begin/callback and webhook ingress routes. Connector initiation is authenticated; callbacks are state-protected; production public origin must be HTTPS and cannot be Base44.

route_registry.boundary: Routes are staged and verified without traffic movement. Activation requires pinned release, binding, probe and explicit cutover receipts; rollback can return a route to verified-but-inactive.

active_route_overlay.boundary: Only active HTTPS routes with cutover authority may enter public discovery. Staged or merely verified candidates remain invisible and legacy public routes persist until explicit cutover.

resident_scheduler.boundary: Cycle and resident work run under an owned supervisor with bounded cadence, restart budgets, idempotent service state and receipt-backed health. Each migrated job still requires product-specific idempotency and parity evidence.

commerce_boundary.boundary: Evercraft verifies provider-authoritative payment state and does not treat checkout creation as payment truth. Payment references are hashed in receipts and card data is not stored.

fabric_discovery.boundary: Owned Fabric discovery is read-only, strips Base44 handoffs from native runtime catalogs and exposes no payment or external-action authority. Product-specific machine surface parity remains required before public route activation.

object_delivery.boundary: Object bytes remain in Evercraft Object Store and are exposed only through short-lived HMAC-signed read URLs. Production origin must be owned HTTPS; raw filesystem paths and permanent public blob URLs are not exposed.
